images.title: A box that multiplies by 6
images.purpose: Show that the number a box multiplies by is a factor of every number that comes out, and that the numbers that come out are multiples of it.
images.composition: A box marked × 6 with the numbers 5, 7 and 9 going in on the left and 30, 42 and 54 coming out on the right, and one sentence under it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. A cardboard box seen from the front in the middle, front rectangle x 548 to 908 and y 330 to 570 (360 by 240 px), filled amber #E69F00 with a 4 px dark #2B2B2B outline; on its front the text × 6 in bold dark #1F2937 (110 px), centred at x 728 and y 450. Its open top is a dark grey #6B7280 parallelogram from x 568 to x 928 at y 290 to 330. On the left, 3 teal #0072B2 rounded-rectangle tags (150 by 90 px, white bold numbers 64 px), one above the other, with the numbers 5, 7 and 9 and centres at x 270 and y 240, 360 and 480; from the right edge of each tag a straight dark arrow (5 px, arrowhead) runs to the box left side at x 548 and y 330, 420 and 510. On the right, 3 reddish purple #CC79A7 rounded-rectangle tags of the same size with the numbers 30, 42 and 54 and centres at x 1190 and y 240, 360 and 480; from the box right side at x 908 and y 330, 420 and 510 a straight dark arrow runs to the left edge of each tag. Under the box, centred at x 728 and y 690, one line of bold dark #1F2937 text, 6 is a factor of 30, 42 and 54 (54 px). The tags and the multiplier are the only numbers in the frame. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: The multiplier 6 is a factor of the numbers that come out, 30, 42 and 54, and they are multiples of 6.
images.description: A box marked times 6: the numbers 5, 7 and 9 go in and 30, 42 and 54 come out.
images.context: Concept image for Factors and Multiples. It follows the idea of the box picture in your maths book and uses the numbers of this concept's own example, a box that multiplies by 6.
images.teaching_notes: Run each number through the box one at a time: 5 × 6 = 30, 7 × 6 = 42, 9 × 6 = 54. The slip to watch is calling the numbers that went in the multiples.

image_decisions.why: The box with the multiplier and the numbers in and out makes factor and multiple visible as one multiplication.
